correctness.rationale: For even \(k\), primes in a consecutive block are odd. If \(p>B(k)\), then \(p\ne\rho(k)\); the least-missing-prime progression lemma forces a composite by index \(\rho(k)-1\). Its largest prime factor is at most one third of the odd composite, giving a next prime \(q\le(p+k(\rho(k)-1))/3<p\). A cycle with all primes above \(B(k)\) would therefore have a strictly decreasing cyclic sequence of prime states, impossible. Disjoint deterministic cycles then inject into the primes at most \(B(k)\). The packaged verifier checks the local inequalities and observed cycles on broad finite ranges.

value.rationale: The bound addresses the harder even-parameter side of the loop-count problem in the source. For every even \(k\ge4\) with \(3\nmid k\), it forces every cycle to meet a prime at most \(k\), giving \(L(k)\le\pi(k)\); for all such \(k\ge8\) this is strictly smaller than the published \(k\sqrt{k}/2\) prime-locator scale. The improvement holds on a natural infinite congruence family and comes from a reusable structural mechanism, not a routine finite increment.
